newsitem.title: GREECE: MILLS ST.GEORGE SAYS 96 PRETAX PROFIT UP 25PCT.
newsitem.headline: MILLS ST.GEORGE SAYS 96 PRETAX PROFIT UP 25PCT.

text.p: Pre-tax earnings of Mills St.George, Greece's largest flour mill, rose 25.4 percent to 1.0 billion drachmas in 1996, while turnover grew 10.8 percent to 16,3 billion drachmas.

The company plans to distribute a per share dividend of 85 drachmas for 1996, up from 65 drachmas a year earlier, managing director Aristides Symeonoglou told Greek institutional investors on Wednesday.
The company operates three flour mills with a total daily capacity of 835 tonnes and makes use of a 34,000-tonne wheat silo and a 6,000-tonne flour silo.
A 1.5 billion drachma modernisation plan which started in 1995 will see completion in June 1997.
Since 1990, Mills St. George has carried out two more investment programmes totalling 3.0 billion drachmas.
Modernisation has resulted in drastic cuts in workforce, currently at 220 -- half its late 1980s level.
Mills St. George plans to introduce branded products and expand its product range to include flour-based frozen food and ready mixes, marketed through super markets.
Currently, St George Mills is the only Greek flour mill selling through super markets, it said.
